question: The stronger base's signed cross-context correction trained on 4061 rows and selected at half share gained 3 and 2 questions on two development panels. Does the identical correction help when the base itself is the nominee of the ordinary search on every fold?
design: Reuse all five previously scored 48-fit regular entries, without changing the base classifier, winner or prior search. Fit a signed offset to at least two disjoint existing inner held panels of each winner. For each panel both the supervised base and response memory exclude all held rows. Verify split indices and exact-feature-group disjointness. At inference, build the response memory on the full outer training partition. If recurring structure is absent on a calibration or full partition, retain the base. No method or field names are supplied to the estimator.
primary: Freeze sum-loss penalty 24, clipped log-odds correction of 1.25 and half probability share from development. Compare to ordinary regular on all 8117 training rows once per row. Save all predictions and verify the original independent solve before opening the five outer answer packets. To justify a future cold ordinary-entry experiment require pooled gain >=.003, at least three positive folds, and no fold below -.003. These previously studied folds are developmental and this study cannot qualify opening the designated validation.
secondary: Compare adding precisely the same offset to the existing unconditional three-seed full-fit probabilities versus the seed blend alone. Freeze the coefficients learned against the original base. Count every small response memory and logistic head, and reuse all original classifier and seed weights. No API, official test or H2.
